en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section The Eighth Chapter
The Discourse on the Strands of Sensual Pleasure: Are the five strands of sensual pleasure the realm of sense-desire? Yes.
Is it not the case that there is desire associated with that [object]?
Yes, it is.
If indeed there is desire associated with that, then surely you should not say:
“The five strands of sensual pleasure are the sense-sphere.

But is it not the case that there is lust associated with them, desire associated with them, desire-and-lust associated with them, intention associated with them, passion associated with them, and intention-and-passion associated with them? And those associated with them—
Is rapture associated with that [feeling] and joy associated with that [feeling] "rapture-and-joy associated with that"?
Yes. If there is rapture-and-joy associated with that, then indeed, it should not be said—
“Only the five strands of sensual pleasure are the realm of sensual desire.
Is it the case that only the five strands of sensual pleasure are the realm of sensual desire?
Yes, it is.
Is the eye of humans not part of the sense-sphere of desire (*kāmadhātu*)?
One should not say so …pe… [the same applies to] the ear of humans …pe…
The nose of human beings … [and so on] … the tongue of human beings … [and so on] … the body of human beings … [and so on].
Is the mind of human beings not the sense-sphere element (kāmadhātu)?
One should not say so … [as before] … Is the mind of human beings not the sense-sphere element?
“Yes.
[The opponent asks: “Has it not been said by the Blessed One:
‘There are five strands of sensual pleasure in the world’?”
The mind is declared to be the sixth;
having detached from desire for this,
one is thus liberated from suffering.
Is it indeed a sutta? Yes.
Therefore, it should not be said—
“Human beings’ mind is not the realm of sensual desire.
Is it the case that only the five strands of sensual pleasure constitute the realm of sensual desire?
Yes, it is.
Are the strands of sensual pleasure, existence, destiny, the abode of beings, saṃsāra, the womb, the station of consciousness, and the acquisition of a personal identity [identical]?
One should not say so... [etc.
...Is there karma that leads to the strands of sensual pleasure?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is it the case that there are beings who go to the realm of sensual pleasures?
It should not be said thus … [as before] …
“Are beings born, age, die, pass away, and reappear because of the strands of sensual pleasure?
“One should not say so.
… “Are there, in the strands of sensual pleasure, form, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness?”
It should not be said so … [as before] … Are the strands of sensual pleasure the five-aggregate existence?
It should not be said so … [as before] …
Is it the case that Fully Enlightened Ones arise in the realm of sensual pleasure (*kāmaguṇa*), Paccekabuddhas arise there, and a pair of disciples arises there?

One should not say so … [and so on] … Is the realm of sensual pleasure existence, a destination, an abode of beings, saṃsāra, a womb, a station of consciousness, or the acquisition of a personal identity?
“Yes,” [you say].

“Are the strands of sensual pleasure (kāmaguṇa) existence (bhava), a destination (gati), an abode of beings (sattāvāsa), saṃsāra, a womb (yoni), a station of consciousness (viññāṇaṭṭhiti), and the acquisition of a personal identity (attabhāvapaṭilābha)?
You should not speak thus …pe…
Is there karma that leads to the sense-sphere realm (*kāmadhātu*)?
Yes. Is there karma that leads to the objects of sensual pleasure (*kāmaguṇa*)? Yes.
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is it the case that there are beings who go to the realm of sensual desire? Yes.

Is it the case that there are beings who go to the realm of sensual pleasures? One should not say so… [as before] … Do beings in the sense-sphere realm (kāmadhātu) take birth, grow old, die, pass away, and reappear?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Are beings born, grow old, die, pass away, and reappear because of attachment to the strands of sensual pleasure?
You should not speak thus …pe…
Is there form, feeling, perception, volitional formations, and consciousness in the sense-sphere realm?
Yes. Is there form, feeling, perception, volitional formations, and consciousness in the objects of sensual pleasure?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is the sense-sphere element (kāmadhātu) fivefold existence (pañcavokārabhava)? Yes.
Are the five strands of sensual pleasure the existence of the fivefold plane?
One should not say so …pe… do perfectly enlightened Buddhas arise in the realm of sense-desire? Do solitary Buddhas arise there? Does a pair of chief disciples arise there?
“Yes,” you say.
“Then do perfectly enlightened Buddhas arise among the strands of sensual pleasure? Do paccekabuddhas arise there? Does a pair of chief disciples arise there?
You must not say so … [and so on] … .
Is it not to be said that "only the five strands of sensual pleasure are the sense-sphere element"?
Yes, it is.
Has it not been said by the Blessed One:
“Bhikkhus, there are these five strands of sensual pleasure.
Which five?”
Forms cognizable by the eye that are desirable, lovely, agreeable, pleasing, connected with sensual desire, and provocative of lust;
sounds cognizable by the ear … smells cognizable by the nose … tastes cognizable by the tongue … [and so forth].
“Tangible objects cognizable by the body that are desirable, lovely, agreeable, pleasing, connected with sensual desire,
and provocative of lust— these, monks, are the five strands of sensual pleasure.
Is there indeed such a sutta?
“Yes.
“In that case, there are only five strands of sensual pleasure and they constitute the sense-sphere realm (kāmadhātu).
The Discussion of the Strands of Sensual Pleasure is finished.
